<result>I stopped without claiming or editing anything. `ddflow_claim` refused DEP-decide (exit 3), and you ruled out `--force`.

- `P-roadmap` has 5 open tasks.
- `P-docs-search` has 9 open tasks.

This is the intended hold. The `P-deprecation` body says "Held behind the docs wave (D-old-work-behind-core-docs-accepted)". The task itself declares no needs, so the claim says it is not ready.

**What I did:**
- Called `ddflow_identify` as `dep-decide`.
- Ran `ddflow_brief`.
- Read `D-compat-r2` and `P-deprecation`.
- Nothing is recorded: no session prompt, no `D-DEP-*` decisions, no doc edits.

I did not record your answers via `ddflow_session_prompt` or `ddflow_decision_add` either. Without a claim, the decisions doc and any task amendments could be overwritten by a parallel agent.

**Decision for you** (pick one; I resume once you do):
1. Tell me to `--force` the claim for this one doc-only item. It writes only `docs/ddflow/decisions/deprecation-lifecycle.md`, so the conflict risk is low.
2. Clear DEP-decide's inherited needs with `ddflow_update` (`needs=""`), if you want the decision wave to run ahead of the docs wave.
3. Leave it held until the three docs phases close.

I filed no bug. As I read it, the hold works as designed, and it only conflicts with a decision-recording step that needs no code. If you think it is a gap, say so and I will file it as a `DX-` task.</result>

OPERATOR ANSWERS (2026-10-22), all equal to the recommended defaults: Q1 two tiers: stable (documented CLI commands/flags, config keys) keeps "until 1.0"; beta (MCP tool names, [enforce] aliases, experimental knobs) two releases AND 30 days; tier added to D-compat-r2. Q2 floors: stable 2 releases + 90 days, beta 2 releases + 30 days, experimental none. Q3 a deprecation record is required for every renamed/removed public name (one per alias family), enforced by version lint. Q4 usage observation opt-in local counters off by default, "no evidence" when nobody opted in. Q5 erroring stage one release before removal, stable tier only. Q6 one short MCP-instructions clause only while a breaking record is in warning or later, within the charter budget. Q7 emit deprecation.due event + rendered message; delivery is an opt-in integration, no network calls from core. Q8 shortening a window needs an expiring recorded waiver with a reason; projects cannot shorten company floors; security exceptions need severity=security and a lesson. Q9 project (customer-facing) deprecations in scope: scope=project, generated DEPRECATIONS.md, notice template, Deprecation/Sunset header text; ddflow sends nothing. Q10 requirement/spec obsolete state computed from the record reaching removed; stories close obsolete; shared state name agreed with RQM-model and SPEC-gate. Q11 event kinds tombstone only (stubs removed at a major only). Q12 retrofit ddflow's own deprecations as records after Q1, one per alias family, Alias.removed_in read from them.

data.alternatives: Supersede D-compat-r2 with the two-release rule everywhere (breaks the until-1.0 promise to CLI/config users). Keep until-1.0 everywhere (contradicts the tool-diet two-release decision and keeps MCP aliases forever).
data.consequences: Every public name needs a tier on its record; the retrofit (DEP-retrofit) assigns tiers; two texts stay valid, each for its tier.
data.context: DEP-decide question; proposal in docs/ddflow/decisions/deprecation-lifecycle.md; answer equals the recommended default.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q1: two tiers. Stable (documented CLI commands/flags, config keys) keeps 'until 1.0'. Beta (MCP tool names, [enforce] aliases, experimental knobs) is removable after two releases AND 30 days. The tier is added to D-compat-r2 (amended, not superseded); D-mcp-tool-families and CM-decide Q12 stay in force for the beta tier.
data.title: Deprecation windows are tiered: stable keeps until 1.0, beta two releases and 30 days (adds a tier to D-compat-r2)

data.alternatives: Calendar date alone (a stalled cadence shortens the window). Release count alone (rapid releases shorten it in time). One floor for all tiers.
data.consequences: Window computation (DEP-lifecycle) needs release dates from version history and a tier-keyed floor table, configurable tighten-only.
data.context: DEP-decide question; proposal in docs/ddflow/decisions/deprecation-lifecycle.md; answer equals the recommended default.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q2: the effective window is the longer of N releases and D days. stable: 2 releases and 90 days (and not before 1.0 for documented CLI/config per Q1); beta: 2 releases and 30 days; experimental: no floor.
data.title: Window floors: stable 2 releases + 90 days, beta 2 releases + 30 days, experimental none

data.alternatives: Per-alias records (noise). Record only when the author remembers (not enforced, against the project rule 'enforced, not requested').
data.consequences: Version lint/cut must diff the public surface against records; DEP-inventory and DEP-retrofit supply the baseline.
data.context: DEP-decide question; proposal in docs/ddflow/decisions/deprecation-lifecycle.md; answer equals the recommended default.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q3: every renamed or removed public name (CLI command/flag, MCP tool/argument, config key, knob, event kind) requires a deprecation record, one per family of aliases not per alias; version lint fails without one.
data.title: A deprecation record is required for every renamed or removed public name, one per alias family, enforced by version lint

data.alternatives: Default-on telemetry (privacy, trust). No observation at all (removal blind).
data.consequences: Removal gate has three outcomes: no recorded use, recorded use, no evidence; the last needs the window alone.
data.context: DEP-decide question; proposal in docs/ddflow/decisions/deprecation-lifecycle.md; answer equals the recommended default.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q4: counters of deprecated-name calls live in a machine-local file, off by default. The removal gate asks for 'no recorded use or a waiver' and reports 'no evidence' when nobody opted in, never 'unused'. Sharing is explicit.
data.title: Usage observation is opt-in local counters, off by default; no data is reported as no evidence

data.alternatives: No erroring stage (removal is the first break). Erroring for all tiers (needless friction for experimental/beta names).
data.consequences: Lifecycle states keep 'erroring' but beta records skip it; stable removal needs an erroring release first.
data.context: DEP-decide question; proposal in docs/ddflow/decisions/deprecation-lifecycle.md; answer equals the recommended default.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q5: stable-tier deprecated paths error (unless --allow-deprecated) for one release before removal; the erroring stage is off for the beta tier.
data.title: An erroring stage precedes removal by one release, stable tier only

data.alternatives: No mention (agents miss the change until a call fails). A list of deprecations in instructions (budget).
data.consequences: Instruction builder must count the clause in the budget test; the clause disappears when no breaking record is active.
data.context: DEP-decide question; proposal in docs/ddflow/decisions/deprecation-lifecycle.md; answer equals the recommended default.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q6: at most one short clause in the MCP instructions, only while a record with severity breaking is in warning or later, inside the LS-charter budget (1.5K chars).
data.title: MCP instructions carry one short deprecation clause only while a breaking record is in warning or later

data.alternatives: Built-in webhook/mail sender (network calls and secrets in core). No event (alerts impossible).
data.consequences: Event schema becomes a contract; integrations live outside core (DEP-notify).
data.context: DEP-decide question; proposal in docs/ddflow/decisions/deprecation-lifecycle.md; answer equals the recommended default.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q7: ddflow emits a deprecation.due hook event and a rendered message; delivery (webhook, chat, mail) is an opt-in integration; core makes no network call.
data.title: Alerts: emit a deprecation.due event and rendered message; delivery is an opt-in integration, no network in core

data.alternatives: Allow maintainers to shorten freely (silent breakage). Forbid all shortening (blocks real security fixes).
data.consequences: A waiver record kind/field with expiry; window gate reads waivers; layering follows D-config-layer-order.
data.context: DEP-decide question; proposal in docs/ddflow/decisions/deprecation-lifecycle.md; answer equals the recommended default.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q8: nobody shortens a window without an expiring recorded waiver with a reason; a project cannot shorten a company floor (tighten-only per D-config-layer-order); a security exception needs severity=security and a recorded lesson.
data.title: Shortening a window needs an expiring recorded waiver; projects cannot shorten company floors; security exceptions need severity=security and a lesson

data.alternatives: ddflow-internal deprecations only (misses the operator's customer-notification ask). ddflow sends notices (network, trust).
data.consequences: Project-scope separation from shipped records is needed (DEP-record, DEP-project); sister-project consumers are told through CN-cr.
data.context: DEP-decide question; proposal in docs/ddflow/decisions/deprecation-lifecycle.md; answer equals the recommended default.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q9: managed projects use the same kind with scope=project; ddflow generates DEPRECATIONS.md, a customer notice template and Deprecation/Sunset header text; ddflow itself sends nothing.
data.title: Project (customer-facing) deprecations are in scope: scope=project, generated DEPRECATIONS.md, notice template, Deprecation/Sunset header text; ddflow sends nothing

data.alternatives: Manual obsolete flag (drifts). Separate lifecycle in requirements/specs (two sources of truth).
data.consequences: DEP-project depends on RQM-model and SPEC-gate agreeing the state name; computed, never stored twice.
data.context: DEP-decide question; proposal in docs/ddflow/decisions/deprecation-lifecycle.md; answer equals the recommended default.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q10: a requirement/spec subject's obsolete state is computed from its deprecation record reaching removed; stories close obsolete. The shared state name is agreed with RQM-model and SPEC-gate (declared dependency).
data.title: Requirement/spec obsolete state is computed from the deprecation record reaching removed; stories close obsolete

data.alternatives: Delete handlers for removed kinds (breaks replay of old logs).
data.consequences: Replay keeps tombstone handlers; major-version cleanup is a recorded decision.
data.context: DEP-decide question; proposal in docs/ddflow/decisions/deprecation-lifecycle.md; answer equals the recommended default.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-22, Q11: removed event kinds stay readable forever (replay); handler stubs and removal stubs for commands/tools are dropped only at a major version, recorded.
data.title: Event kinds are tombstoned, never deleted; stubs removed at a major only

data.alternatives: Leave code tables as truth (two sources). One record per alias (noise).
data.consequences: DEP-retrofit follows DEP-record; code tables become generated/checked against records; tier assigned per Q1.
data.context: DEP-decide question; proposal in docs/ddflow/decisions/deprecation-lifecycle.md; answer equals the recommended default.
